The site is St. Jude’s Chamber Music — Acoustic Concert Pew Reservation, a booking web application for Parish church acoustic concert seat selection.

Owner brief: "Our parish church holds acoustic chamber music evenings with allocated pew seating, but our booking form loses reservations upon refresh and cannot be navigated without a mouse. Repair the booking application so reservations are saved on the server, interactive pew seats are accessible by keyboard with visible focus rings, and empty submissions are caught with clear feedback."

Locale & copy conventions (en-GB): Use £ prices, British English spelling, day-month dates and .co.uk-style invented domains. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-27/reference.jpg).

Art direction: St. Jude’s Chamber Music — Acoustic Concert Pew Reservation: the page for parish church acoustic concert seat selection, in a light palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #44403c (sj-stone), #831843 (sj-ruby), #d97706 (sj-gold), #ffffff (sj-card), #e7e5e4 (sj-border), #fafaf9 (sj-bg), #1c1917 (sj-text), #78716c (sj-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 8px, content-frame 1200px, control-border 1px solid var(--sj-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a calendar widget that hides the available slots behind extra clicks; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of St. Jude’s Chamber Music — Acoustic Concert Pew Reservation as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Attendee name", "Email address", "Contact telephone", "Number of seats", "Pew section").

User journey context: View church seating layout and choose an available pew section for an upcoming concert. Enter attendee name and contact details, and submit the seat reservation. Receive the booking voucher with pew reference and reload the browser to ensure the seat is preserved.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
